sentence: This project studies how both processes inside the body and harmful chemicals in the environment cause the mutation patterns seen in cancer.
This project studies in people and in animal models how hearing loss at very high frequencies and cognitive decline affect understanding speech in background noise.
This project provides research experiences at the meeting point of nanotechnology, cancer biology, and medicine.
This project provides lab services that measure toxic chemicals, metals, pesticides, and other environmental exposures in human, model system, and environmental samples.
This project tries to find out how a connective tissue growth factor drives muscle loss in pancreatic cancer patients with cachexia.
This project builds computer tools that read clinical notes and surveys to find social factors and substance use disorders in patients.
This project develops and makes a fluorescent imaging agent that marks proteins in developing melanomas so they can be found early.
This project creates two strains of laboratory mice that can be used to test how safe and effective base editing therapies are.
This project studies how a form of tumor suppression called overdominant works in lung cancer, using CRISPR and mouse models.
This project builds computer methods that use machine learning to predict how genomic variation matters and to combine genomic data in studies of human diseases.
This project tests and improves the manufacturing of a gene editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
This project tries to find out how creatine feeds the low-oxygen area of glioblastoma and whether blocking creatine use can slow tumor growth.
This project provides lab tests that find the cell and genome features of gastric precursors at high risk of turning into cancer.
This project studies how brain cells change during human development and how genetic variation and DNA sequence elements affect that process.
This project builds a swine model of pancreatic cancer to test adenoviruses that are given through the blood to find and treat the cancer.
This project works toward better ways to prevent, detect early, and treat cancer.
This project studies how changes in chromatin and a protein activity help revival stem cells form and repair the intestine after radiation injury.
This project tries to find out how a memory of ethanol exposure is started and passed to later generations through epigenetic and metabolic changes.
This project builds MRI imaging methods that give clearer and more consistent images of brain tumors across different scanners.
This project uses human stem cells, tissue engineering, animal models, and single-cell analysis to find out what causes cardiac fibrosis.
